endorsements.quote: Chirurgie 4.0 proposes five steps that can genuinely be climbed and a method for deciding, on the basis of evidence, how to climb them safely, with the surgeon retaining final clinical authority at every rung.
The operating room is safe only when the level of autonomy of every tool within it is named, evaluated, and governed.
and agent governance, which sets the permissions, safety limits, and escalation rules for AI agents.

unlisted_practices: Establish a national early-access pathway for digital, robotic, and algorithmic innovations with provisional nomenclature and tariff and a three-year experimental registry.
Move from centralized to distributed evaluation of intelligent surgical technologies in accredited centers.
Recognize and fund clinical registries as strategic national infrastructure.
Evolve the national health technology assessment body into an augmented body able to evaluate devices that learn.
Create a national observatory of surgical and interventional innovations to map the sector.
Build governance natively into learning surgical AI systems through a Cognitive Governance Layer of human oversight, explainability, auditability, and agent governance.
Treat operating room cybersecurity as a condition of clinical legitimacy for learning operating rooms.
Declare, evaluate, supervise, and revise the autonomy level of each surgical technology on an explicit autonomy scale.
License autonomous clinical AI and continuously reassess it rather than approving it once as a device.

screen.reason: This is a perspective/framework paper introducing the Chirurgie 4.0 maturity model and governance recommendations for AI and surgical world models in the operating room.
